subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should this umbrella stay open until both the high-frequency warning and cron-session retention slices are resolved, or should maintainers split the remaining guardrails into narrower canonical issues now?
rationale: The source-backed gaps are real, but the warning threshold, context-warning policy, and base-session cleanup semantics are compatibility-sensitive product choices rather than one safe automatic repair.

options.title: Keep Open For Linked Slices
options.body: Use this issue as the umbrella while maintainers decide the warning and retention PR paths, then split any leftover context-threshold or sessions-cleanup work.

options.title: Split Remaining Guardrails
options.body: Create or confirm narrower canonical issues for context-threshold warnings and `sessions cleanup`, and let each PR close only its own slice.

options.title: Reject Fixed Warning Threshold
options.body: If a fixed sub-30-minute advisory is not desired, close or narrow the warning path and keep retention cleanup as the primary bug track.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Linked Slices
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the umbrella while maintainers decide the warning and retention PR paths, then split any leftover context-threshold or sessions-cleanup work.

likelyOwner.reason: The most consequential unresolved choice is the cron/session lifecycle boundary introduced in the reaper path and now challenged by base-session retention reports.
